papers.title: Prompt versus Delayed Triple Therapy in COPD: Solutions to Time-Related Biases in Observational Studies.
papers.one_line: Cloning 91,958 CPRD patients with a COPD exacerbation into prompt and delayed triple-therapy arms gave a hazard ratio of 0.98 (95% CI 0.80 to 1.19) for a subsequent exacerbation, against 0.73 (0.65 to 0.81) when the published design that defines exposure by looking forward is replicated.
papers.what_was_done: A cohort of 91,958 patients with COPD and a moderate or severe exacerbation after September 2017 was assembled from the UK Clinical Practice Research Datalink. Each patient was cloned into a prompt arm (single-inhaler triple therapy within 30 days of the index exacerbation) and a delayed arm (initiation between days 31 and 180), giving 91,958 clones per arm, with artificial censoring when observed treatment became incompatible with the assigned strategy and inverse probability of censoring weights fit by pooled logistic regression at day 30, at the index date, between days 1 and 30, and at day 180. Only prompt initiators starting between days 16 and 30, and delayed initiators between days 152 and 180, were upweighted to stand in for the clones censored at the boundary. Confidence intervals came from a 1,000-sample nonparametric bootstrap. Unweighted incidence rates of a first exacerbation were 0.217 and 0.130 per person-month in the prompt and delayed clone sets; after censoring weights they were 0.101 and 0.103, giving a hazard ratio of 0.98 (95% CI 0.80 to 1.19), and 1.26 (0.81 to 1.96) for severe exacerbation. Replicating the published design on 2,650 initiators gave 0.73 (0.65 to 0.81) and 0.58 (0.46 to 0.74). Only 4,876 of 91,958 patients initiated single-inhaler triple therapy within 180 days.

future_research.gap: Exposure timing is misclassified by the gap between prescription and actual initiation, and censoring weights computed from observed timing cannot correct it.
future_research.quote: The use of censoring weights, however, because they are calculated using the observed exposure timing, does not account for this misclassification.

problems.evidence: The 30-day and 180-day boundaries that define the two strategies are inherited from the studies being criticized, with no outcome-blind rule justifying either. The choice is not innocuous: prescription dates lag actual initiation, so the shorter prompt window absorbs the misclassification asymmetrically, and the entire contrast between 0.98 and 0.73 turns on which side of day 30 a patient lands.
problems.quote: Thus, the 30- and 180-day thresholds used to define prompt and delayed treatment will necessarily be affected by this misclassification, which should differentially affect the shorter prompt treatment period.

problems.evidence: The reported hazard ratio of 0.98 is a censoring-weighted contrast in which the clones surviving to the strategy boundary are represented by a narrow slice of initiators: only those starting between days 16 and 30 were upweighted to replace clones censored at day 30, and only those starting between days 152 and 180 to replace clones censored at day 180. What is reported is a Cox hazard ratio; what is estimated is a weighted per-protocol contrast carried by a boundary-compatible subgroup of a cohort in which 87,082 of 91,958 patients never initiated at all.
problems.quote: Only prompt initiators starting treatment between day 16 and 30 were upweighted to replace clones censored on day 30.

problems.evidence: Cloning is presented as retiring confounding outright, on the ground that the two arms contain the same replicated people. The claim does not survive the design's own machinery: three separate censoring weight models were needed precisely because artificial censoring is informative, and their validity rests on the measured baseline covariates listed in Table 1. The emulation label is doing work that the identification argument does not support.
problems.quote: Indeed, this approach is not affected by confounding as the cloning results in the same patients being replicated, making the two comparison groups identical on all subject characteristics.

problems.evidence: Cloning turned 91,958 patients into 183,916 correlated clone records, and the only variance route offered is a 1,000-sample nonparametric bootstrap over the whole weighted, cloned, time-varying-weight pipeline. No analytic or sandwich alternative is given, and the cost scales with the cohort rather than with the 4,876 patients who actually initiated. The default is correct and expensive, which is the shape of the open problem.
problems.quote: The corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CI) for the hazard ratios were obtained using the non-parametric bootstrap method based on 1000 random samples.

problems.evidence: The two strategies are defined purely by initiation timing of single-inhaler triple therapy, and patients who reached the same pharmacological state through three separate inhalers were censored rather than counted as treated. Whether same-day LABA, LAMA and ICS prescriptions belong in the same equivalence class as the single inhaler is decided by the censoring rule, not by any stated clinical criterion, and that decision moves person-time out of both arms.
problems.quote: In addition to the artificial censoring associated with the cloning process, patients were also censored when they initiated triple therapy in multiple inhalers

problems.evidence: The outcome carrying the headline estimate is a phenotype: a moderate exacerbation is a prednisolone prescription and a severe one an ICD-10 hospitalization code. Both enter the weighted Cox model as error-free binary events, and the acknowledged misclassification of the prednisolone rule is not propagated into the 95% CI of 0.80 to 1.19 or into any quantitative bias analysis.
problems.quote: the outcome of a moderate exacerbation is defined only based on a prescription for prednisolone which, while a common practice in the UK, could introduce some misclassification

papers.title: Machine Learning Versus Logistic Regression for Propensity Score Estimation: A Benchmark Trial Emulation Against the PARADIGM-HF Randomized Trial.
papers.one_line: Three propensity score strategies applied to the same VA cohort of 583 sacubitril/valsartan initiators and 1,864 ACEI/ARB users produced hazard ratios of 0.93, 0.97 and 0.61 against a trial benchmark of 0.81, with the most predictive model (AUC 0.95) the furthest from the trial.
papers.what_was_done: A device-stratified secondary analysis of PARADIGM-HF, in which sacubitril/valsartan carried a 19% lower risk of all-cause mortality than enalapril among 1,243 participants with an ICD or CRT-D (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.61 to 1.06), was emulated in VA Corporate Data Warehouse records from 2016 to 2020. Eligibility required heart failure, ejection fraction at or below 35%, an implanted device, and a natriuretic peptide threshold; 583 sacubitril/valsartan initiators and 1,864 ACEI/ARB users were analyzed with a median follow-up of 23 months. Three propensity score models were fit on identical data: logistic regression on prespecified confounders (AUC 0.79; HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.61 to 1.42), generalized boosted models on the same confounders with hyperparameters tuned by 10-fold cross-validation (AUC 0.81; HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.68 to 1.37), and generalized boosted models with 14 extra predictors and automated feature selection (AUC 0.95, 95% CI 0.94 to 0.97; HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.30 to 1.23). Under the third model the median predicted probability of treatment was 0.934 in the treated group and 0.042 in the comparator group. Two overadjustment paths were diagnosed by directed acyclic graph: albumin as a collider and time since device implantation as a near-instrument. Under the second model, beta-blockers and SGLT2 inhibitors were dropped from every boosted tree despite being class 1A therapies. New York Heart Association class, a trial eligibility criterion, was absent from the electronic record, and no transportability analysis was run.

future_research.gap: Benchmarking was informal; the trial effect was never formally transported to the study sample because individual-level trial data were unavailable.
future_research.quote: without access to individual-level trial data, we could not formally transport the trial result to our study sample

problems.evidence: The comparison isolates flexibility from identification: the boosted model with the largest covariate set and the best treatment discrimination (AUC 0.95) produced the estimate furthest from the trial (HR 0.61 versus 0.81), while ordinary logistic regression on a hand-chosen confounder set came closest (HR 0.93). Algorithmic flexibility addressed functional-form misspecification and left causal-structure misspecification untouched, with a collider and a near-instrument entering the adjustment set.
problems.quote: Our findings suggest that ML-based propensity score methods do not inherently improve causal estimation

problems.evidence: Nuisance-model tuning ran over a grid of shrinkage, interaction depth and minimum node size selected by 10-fold cross-validation error, an objective that rewards discrimination between treated and untreated. The tuned model reached AUC 0.81 and then 0.95 with additional predictors, and its causal estimate moved away from the trial as its predictive performance improved. The paper states that the classification metric is not relevant to causal inference and can mislead when read as evidence of confounding control, yet no alternative selection criterion is supplied.
problems.quote: Hyperparameters, including shrinkage (0.3, 0.1, 0.05, 0.01 and 0.005), interaction.depth (2, 3, 5 and 7) and n.minobsinnode (10, 20, 30, 50, 75, 100 and 150) were tuned based on 10-fold cross-validation errors.

problems.evidence: The positivity failure under the third model is reported as a pair of median predicted probabilities, 0.934 in the treated group against 0.042 in the comparator, and as a histogram described as barely overlapping. No patient history is named as unsupported, no trimming or truncation rule was triggered, and the analysis proceeded to a hazard ratio of 0.61 with a confidence interval spanning 0.30 to 1.23. The diagnostic described the weight distribution and did not identify which covariate patterns had no comparator.
problems.quote: The median [IQR] predicted probability of receiving sacubitril/valsartan was 0.934 [0.629 – 0.996] in the sacubitril/valsartan group and 0.042 [0.022 – 0.087] in the ACEI/ARB group.
problems.locator: Estimates From GBM-Based Propensity Score with Additional Predictors

problems.evidence: New York Heart Association functional class was a trial eligibility criterion and does not exist in the electronic record, so every veteran in the cohort was treated as satisfying it. The emulated population therefore contains patients the trial would have excluded, and the size of that contamination cannot be estimated from the same data. The device-implantation indication, primary versus secondary prevention, was also unavailable.
problems.quote: For instance, the New York Heart Association (NYHA) Functional Classifications, a key eligibility criterion in the trial, was not captured in our EHR data.

problems.evidence: The emulated sample differs from the trial subgroup on every reported axis: mean age 69.8 versus 64.6 years, 1.6% versus 13.5% female, 20.1% versus 6.8% Black, hypertension in 97.3% versus 67.5%. The trial-versus-emulation comparison is nevertheless read as evidence about the adjustment method, with no accounting for the sampling assumptions that would be needed to transport the trial effect onto this case mix.
problems.quote: we only conducted informal benchmarking without transportability analyses

problems.evidence: Three estimators were run on one dataset and the spread was reported: HR 0.93, 0.97 and 0.61 with risk ratios of 0.86, 0.96 and 0.69. That is the demonstration the registry entry says studies are not required to provide, and it shows the choice mattered by a factor larger than any reported confidence interval width would suggest. It does not supply a rule for choosing: the winner is identified only by proximity to a trial result that will usually be unavailable, and the boosted model silently dropped beta-blockers and SGLT2 inhibitors from every tree.
problems.quote: Gender, ethnicity, baseline hypertension and prescription of β-blockers and SGLT2i were not used in any boosted trees.
problems.locator: Estimates From Pre-Specified Confounders and GBM-Based Propensity Score

papers.title: Improving the validity of noninterventional comparative effectiveness research by basing study design on a specified existing randomized controlled trial.
papers.one_line: A commentary on three AJE reference-trial studies distinguishes emulation of a named existing RCT from emulation of a hypothetical target trial, and reports that of thirteen benchmarked oncology emulations only two were rated moderate risk of bias under ROBINS-I while eleven were serious or critical.
papers.what_was_done: Reference trial emulation is set out as a two-part procedure: an existing named RCT informs the observational design, and the observational estimate is then benchmarked against the trial result before analysis is extended to groups the trial excluded. Five specific pitfalls are enumerated. Success criteria vary across the literature and include a limit on the standardized difference of effect estimates, binary agreement metrics, prespecified ranges for the estimate and confidence interval, and informal benchmarking based on whether the same clinical decision would follow. Benchmarking failure is attributed to intractable confounding, differences in the distribution of effect measure modifiers, measurement error and random error, and the commentary argues that a failure should be diagnosed rather than discarded. A systematic review in the same issue assessed thirteen oncology emulations on benchmarking success and on ROBINS-I risk of bias: only two were moderate risk, eleven were serious or critical, and some of the serious or critical studies were judged to have benchmarked successfully. In one of the companion analyses, only two of three COPD reference trials benchmarked successfully, and the failure was traced to forced discontinuation of baseline therapy in the trials, a design feature that cannot be reproduced in routine data. A seven-item reporting table is proposed covering the trial description, prespecified benchmarking criteria, prespecified sensitivity analyses and exploration of benchmarking failure.

future_research.gap: No guidance exists for the conduct and reporting of observational studies whose design is informed by a named reference trial, beyond the seven suggested items.
future_research.quote: further work to develop more detailed guidance on the conduct and reporting of non-interventional studies informed by a reference trial would be valuable
future_research.locator: Reference trials, hypothetical target trials, and real-world evidence

future_research.gap: Bias tools assess emulations against a hypothetical target trial and have no items for the features specific to designing on an actual RCT.
future_research.quote: the ROBINS-I tool is specifically for assessing risk of bias against a hypothetical target trial, and does not include aspects specific to basing non-interventional design on an actual RCT
future_research.locator: Pitfalls of reference trial-informed study design

problems.evidence: Extension after successful benchmarking is presented as the payoff of the design, yet the commentary states that the confounding structure in the extended population need not match the one that was validated, giving the statin example in which sex is a confounder in the benchmarking step but not in an older extended population. It further notes that only a small subset of questions have an appropriate reference trial at all. Nothing licenses the transfer of a validated design from the benchmarked question to the new one.
problems.quote: if extending the analysis to a new target population following successful benchmarking against a reference trial, researchers need to be aware that the confounding structures in the trial and in the new, extended target population may not always be the same
problems.locator: Pitfalls of reference trial-informed study design

problems.evidence: The commentary catalogs the incompatible success measures in use, from standardized-difference limits to binary agreement metrics to informal benchmarking, and rejects reliance on any single metric because agreement depends on the trial's precision and the emulation's sample size. It asks instead that the relative distributions of the two estimates be compared and that conflicts between multiple criteria be resolved a priori. It supplies no calibration statistic and still resolves to a pass or fail verdict, so the estimand comparison remains uncalibrated.
problems.quote: Assessing the compatibility between the results of the RCT and its emulation using a single metric is not recommended
problems.locator: Pitfalls of reference trial-informed study design

problems.evidence: The commentary names the exact mechanism by which the target trial is selected after the data are seen: when the reference result is already known, a team can tune eligibility, variable coding and sensitivity analyses until agreement is reached, and without a prespecified protocol a reader cannot tell that this happened. The proposed remedy is prespecification of the discrepancy-investigation strategy before the first attempt, which acknowledges rather than removes the conditioning problem.
problems.quote: if criteria for successful benchmarking and a detailed analysis approach are not prespecified (e.g. in a protocol), then it is difficult to assess if researchers have modified their study design after comparing their own initial results against those of the reference trial to increase their probability of success
problems.locator: Pitfalls of reference trial-informed study design

problems.evidence: Item 7 of the reporting table asks explicitly that post-hoc analyses run after a benchmarking failure be reported alongside the reasons explored, which would make some of the rejected analytic path visible. The recommendation is voluntary, applies only when benchmarking fails, and covers analyses run after the fact rather than protocol variants considered and dropped before the first estimate.
problems.quote: If unsuccessful, potential reasons should be explored, including any post-hoc analyses done to help elucidate these reasons.

problems.evidence: The thirteen-study oncology review shows the label and the assumption burden coming apart: eleven of thirteen benchmarked emulations carried serious or critical ROBINS-I risk of bias, and studies in that group were nonetheless recorded as having benchmarked successfully. Agreement with a trial result is therefore being read as evidence about design quality when the two were measured independently and disagreed.
problems.quote: there were a number of studies rated as having serious or critical bias that were considered to have successfully benchmarked against the corresponding reference trial
problems.locator: Pitfalls of reference trial-informed study design

problems.evidence: Regulators are told that a benchmarked study warrants greater confidence than one based on a hypothetical target trial, but the commentary simultaneously records that the standard bias instrument has no items for reference-trial-specific features such as differences in trial versus real-world adherence. Diagnosable agreement with a trial and undiagnosable residual confounding are therefore presented to a decision maker through the same single verdict.
problems.quote: Successful benchmarking against a reference trial can improve our confidence in findings from studies using non-interventional data, but it is not an ironclad guarantee of unbiased results.
problems.locator: Pitfalls of reference trial-informed study design

papers.title: Effectiveness and risk of ARB and ACEi among different ethnic groups in England: A reference trial (ONTARGET) emulation analysis using UK Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum-linked data.
papers.one_line: An ONTARGET emulation in 17,593 Black, 30,805 South Asian and 524,623 White patients failed one of two prespecified benchmarking criteria purely on precision, and was declared benchmarked after a random subsample of trial size was analyzed instead.
papers.what_was_done: Courses of ACE inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker therapy in CPRD Aurum from 2001 to 2019, linked to hospital and mortality data, were split into exposed periods separated by treatment gaps over 90 days; trial criteria were applied to the start of each period, one eligible period was drawn at random per patient, and ethnicity-stratified propensity scores were trimmed at the first and ninety-ninth percentiles before inverse probability weighting. Median follow-up was 5.2 years. For the primary composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke or heart failure hospitalization, 27,327 (18.0%) events occurred on ARB and 80,624 (19.1%) on ACEi, giving a hazard ratio of 0.96 (95% CI 0.95 to 0.98) against the trial's 1.01 (0.94 to 1.09). Two validation criteria had been prespecified, that the hazard ratio fall between 0.92 and 1.13 and that its interval contain 1; the first was met and the second was not, so a random subset of 17,687 patients matching trial size was analyzed and returned 0.97 (0.89 to 1.06). Extension by ethnicity found heterogeneity for cardiovascular death (P interaction 0.002): 1.20 (1.02 to 1.40) in Black patients with number needed to harm 93, 0.91 (0.88 to 0.93) in White patients, 0.97 (0.86 to 1.09) in South Asian patients. Angioedema showed no relative heterogeneity but an additive difference, numbers needed to treat 204 versus 1,667. Death censored 9.2% and practice transfer 32%.

future_research.gap: No guidance exists for setting benchmarking criteria when the emulation is far larger than the trial, which is the case that broke the criterion here.
future_research.quote: As these methods are more commonly implemented, we anticipate guidance arising in setting benchmarking criteria.

future_research.gap: The per-protocol effect could not be re-estimated in the trial for comparison because trial outcome data were unavailable.
future_research.quote: However, as we did not have access to the outcome data from ONTARGET, we were unable to estimate this effect in the RCT.

problems.evidence: The benchmarking rule combined a range criterion with a criterion that the interval contain the null, and the second failed for a reason unrelated to agreement: with 570,000 patients the interval on 0.96 was 0.95 to 0.98, narrower than any trial could produce. The verdict is binary and one of its two components measures precision rather than concordance, so a more informative study fails a test that a smaller one passes. No statistic reports how far 0.96 sits from the trial's 1.01 relative to their joint uncertainty.
problems.quote: meeting the first of 2 prespecified validation criteria of confirming similarity to the ONTARGET trial (HR 1.01 (95% CI: 0.94, 1.09)) but not the second, because the CI did not include 1
problems.locator: Benchmarking CPRD Aurum results against the ONTARGET trial results

problems.evidence: When the prespecified criterion failed, a new analysis was constructed after the fact: a random subset of 17,687 patients chosen to match trial size, which passed. The subsequent ethnicity analyses are conditioned on that rescue, and the paper concedes it should have set the confidence-bound criterion with the sample size in mind. The target trial the inference conditions on is thus the one selected after the first estimate was seen.
problems.quote: Due to the much larger size of the observational study, we analysed a randomly selected subset of the cohort consistent with the trial size ( n = 17,687), which gave results consistent with ONTARGET
problems.locator: Benchmarking CPRD Aurum results against the ONTARGET trial results

problems.evidence: The subgroup that drives the clinical conclusion is the smallest and the least supported: 17,593 Black patients against 524,623 White patients, with the Black estimate for the primary outcome spanning 0.93 to 1.12 while the White estimate spans 0.95 to 0.98. The recommendation to revisit UK guidance rests on a cardiovascular death hazard ratio of 1.20 (1.02 to 1.40) in that group, and the paper itself notes that blood pressure estimates in Black patients carry wide intervals. Overlap and precision are worst exactly where the protected-characteristic subgroup effect is being read.
problems.quote: This could be due to differences in sample size between the ethnic groups or due to heterogeneity within ethnic groups.

problems.evidence: Positivity is handled by trimming the propensity score at the first percentile in one arm and the ninety-ninth in the other, a rule stated in terms of weight magnitude and applied within each ethnicity stratum. No covariate pattern is named as having no comparator, and the discarded 1% is not characterized, which matters because the ethnicity strata differ by a factor of thirty in size and the trimming operates separately inside each.
problems.quote: Propensity scores were trimmed at the 1st percentile in the ACEi group and the 99th percentile in the ARB group to avoid extreme weights and violation of the positivity assumption

problems.evidence: Death censors 9.2% of patients in a 5.5-year study whose outcomes include myocardial infarction, stroke and heart failure hospitalization, and it is reported in the same sentence as administrative loss to follow-up at 32%, as though the two were the same kind of event. No identifying assumption is stated for what the non-fatal outcome hazard means after death, and the heterogeneity that drives the paper's conclusion is in cardiovascular death itself, so the censoring and the estimand interact directly.
problems.quote: About 9.2% of patients were censored at death and 32% were censored at transferred out of practice or practice last collection date.

problems.evidence: The design generates repeated eligibility by construction, since a patient with a treatment gap over 90 days starts a new exposed period and can qualify more than once. Repeated participation is then removed by drawing a single eligible period at random per patient, which is a clean fix for the correlation problem and costs the efficiency the sequential design was meant to buy. Calendar-time confounding over an 18-year accrual window is handled only by including time-related variables in the propensity score, not by matching or stratifying on entry date.
problems.quote: Therefore, a patient could contribute multiple eligible exposed periods, as in a trial a patient could meet the trial criteria on more than one occasion.

papers.title: Feasibility of using real-world data to emulate substance use disorder clinical trials: a cross-sectional study.
papers.one_line: Across 272 registered substance use disorder trials with posted results, not one had indications, interventions, at least 80% of eligibility criteria, comparators and primary endpoints all ascertainable from contemporary claims or structured electronic records.
papers.what_was_done: Every phase 2 to 4 trial of a substance use disorder treatment registered on ClinicalTrials.gov with reported results was screened, 272 in total, most for alcohol use disorder (103, 37.9%), stimulant use disorder (68, 25.0%) or opioid use disorder (37, 13.6%). Five protocol components were scored as ascertainable or not from administrative claims and structured fields in two Epic-based electronic record systems, with an 80% threshold for eligibility criteria. Indications were ascertainable in 262 trials (96.3%) and interventions in 194 (71.3%), but the intervention rate splits sharply by modality: 91% of drug trials, 17.6% of behavioral trials and 9.8% of combined drug and behavioral trials. Comparators were ascertainable in 16 of 244 trials with a comparator (5.9%), with 191 of the failures being placebo arms. Primary endpoints were ascertainable in 61 (22.4%); half the failures were endpoints quantifying amount or frequency of substance use and a quarter used timeline follow-back. The unascertainable eligibility criteria were led by breastfeeding status (63.2%), a specific recent use pattern such as cocaine at least four times in the past week (56.3%) and conditional modifiers such as active or uncontrolled disease (45.6%). No trial passed all five. Relaxing the eligibility threshold to 50% left one trial; treating placebo as ascertainable left six (2.2%). Ascertainability was judged from clinical experience with the two systems rather than measured, and unstructured text was excluded.

future_research.gap: Whether natural language processing can recover the protocol components that structured fields miss is untested.
future_research.quote: Further work on trial emulation can also investigate the utilization of rapidly developing tools such as NLP, which represent a promising avenue to better leverage existing RWD.

problems.evidence: The criteria that routine data cannot express are counted rather than asserted: breastfeeding status in 174 of 272 trials, a specific recent substance use pattern in 153, and conditional modifiers such as active or uncontrolled disease in 124. Each is a criterion an emulation would have to either drop or infer, and in either case a patient with no record is treated identically to a patient assessed and found eligible. Only 35 of 272 trials cleared even an 80% bar.
problems.quote: The most common eligibility criteria that were classified as not ascertainable were breastfeeding status (174/272, 63.2%), having a specific pattern of recent substance use (e.g., using cocaine at least 4 times in the past week; 153/272, 56.3%), and conditional modifiers (e.g., uncontrolled disease, active disease; 124/272, 45.6%).

problems.evidence: The routine response to an unascertainable protocol component is documented as omission or modification of the criterion, which silently redefines the population rather than adding noise to it. Here the components at issue are not peripheral: the comparator fails in 228 of 244 trials, mostly because it is a placebo, and the primary endpoint fails in 211 of 272, mostly because it quantifies substance use. An emulation that proceeds anyway is estimating a different, data-defined contrast on a different outcome.
problems.quote: recent published target trial emulations have highlighted the need to omit or modify eligibility criteria in order to successfully conduct their analyses

problems.evidence: The ascertainability of an intervention collapses as soon as it stops being a dispensed drug: 91% for drug trials against 17.6% for behavioral trials and 9.8% for combined drug and behavioral trials. Behavioral treatment for substance use disorder has no national drug code and no reliable procedure code, so neither the treatment version nor the unit at which it is assigned can be recovered from claims. The 51 combined trials fare worst, which is where the intervention is a package rather than a molecule.
problems.quote: Stratified across the various intervention modalities, 91% (183/201) of trials with a drug intervention, 9.8% (5/51) of trials with a combination of drug and behavioral interventions, and 17.6% (3/17) of trials with a behavioral intervention were considered ascertainable with respect to the intervention

problems.evidence: This is a stopping rule with a number in it: five protocol components must be recoverable, eligibility must clear 80% of criteria, and the rule stopped all 272 candidate emulations, with sensitivity analyses at a 50% threshold and with placebo counted as ascertainable leaving one and six. It closes the pre-study half of the entry. It does not close the rest: ascertainability was judged from clinical experience rather than measured against field-completion rates, unstructured text was excluded by construction, and nothing in the screen bears on residual confounding or on data fitness once a study is underway.
problems.quote: For a trial to be considered to have eligibility criteria ascertainable from contemporary claims and/or structured EHR data, it had to have greater than 80% of its total criteria deemed ascertainable.

problems.evidence: The whole screen turns on whether a structured field exists and is populated, and the judgment came from two institutions running the same vendor system. A field can exist in the schema and be filled at wildly different rates by different clinicians and settings, so structural presence does not establish that the variable carries the same meaning across sites. This is the scoring instrument's own acknowledged weak point, and it sits upstream of every count in the paper.
problems.quote: some of these data may be captured at varying rates across clinicians and health care settings

problems.evidence: The endpoints that survive the screen are the ones a code can carry: urinalysis or toxicology results in 69 trials and receipt of a medication in 10, while endpoints quantifying amount or frequency of use fail in 136 of 272. An emulation restricted to codeable endpoints substitutes a binary laboratory phenotype for a graded behavioral measure, and that substitution enters downstream analyses as an error-free outcome with no validation study attached.
problems.quote: The most common end points that were considered not ascertainable were end points that quantified a specific amount or frequency of substance use in a given time period (136, 50.0%)

papers.title: Comparison of oral anticoagulants for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation using the UK clinical practice research Datalink Aurum: A reference trial (ARISTOTLE) emulation study.
papers.one_line: An ARISTOTLE emulation in 8,846 matched apixaban and warfarin pairs met its prespecified benchmarking criteria with a stroke or systemic embolism hazard ratio of 0.98 (95% CI 0.82 to 1.19) against the trial's 0.79 (0.66 to 0.95), losing superiority entirely.
papers.what_was_done: Patients with atrial fibrillation prescribed apixaban or warfarin in CPRD Aurum between January 2013 and July 2019 were selected: 86,888 and 159,632 respectively, reduced to 41,487 and 101,159 after ARISTOTLE inclusion and exclusion criteria. Coarsened exact matching against published trial aggregate characteristics produced 9,120 trial-analogous apixaban patients, of whom 274 (3.0%) failed propensity score matching, leaving 8,846 pairs matched within strata of prior vitamin K antagonist exposure to a maximum standardized difference of 0.031. Benchmarking criteria were prespecified and published: the stroke or systemic embolism hazard ratio had to fall between 0.69 and 0.99 with an upper confidence limit below the trial's 1.38 noninferiority margin. The observed hazard ratio was 0.98 (0.82 to 1.19), meeting noninferiority but not superiority, with all-cause death 1.03 (0.93 to 1.14) against the trial's 0.89. Apixaban absolute event rates matched the trial exactly at 1.27% per year while warfarin ran lower, 1.29% against 1.60%. Time in therapeutic range was higher than in the trial (median 0.76 versus 0.66); against well-controlled warfarin apixaban carried an increased hazard of death, 1.20 (1.04 to 1.37). The cohort held 2.4% Asian patients against 14.4% in the trial, aspirin use 5.8% against 31.3%, and 13.3% of warfarin users had no INR measurement, receiving a predicted value.

future_research.gap: Long-term agreement between the emulation and the trial has not been assessed; follow-up here averaged under 2.2 years.
future_research.quote: We also recommend future analyses with an extended follow-up period compared with this study to compare the long-term outcomes seen in the noninterventional cohort with projected long-term outcomes from the RCT.

problems.evidence: The benchmarking rule is numeric, published in advance and deliberately asymmetric around the trial estimate, and absolute event rates are reported side by side, so the comparison goes beyond a bare label. The verdict is still binary and it passes on an estimate of 0.98 whose confidence interval excludes the trial point estimate of 0.79: the trial showed superiority and the emulation did not, yet both the range criterion and the noninferiority criterion were satisfied. Nothing in the reported comparison quantifies how far the two estimands are apart.
problems.quote: The effect size must be clinically comparable with the ARISTOTLE findings; the HR for time to stroke/SE with the HR must be between 0.69 and 0.99.

problems.evidence: Sixteen percent of warfarin users switched to another oral anticoagulant during follow-up against six percent of apixaban users, and mean follow-up differed between arms at 2.2 versus 1.8 years. The comparator arm therefore converges toward the index treatment as follow-up lengthens, which attenuates the intention-to-treat analogue exactly where the trial reported superiority. The paper adds that patients remaining on warfarin over time are increasingly those doing well on it, and an on-treatment censoring sensitivity analysis showed attrition bias.
problems.quote: A higher proportion of warfarin users switched to alternative OAC during follow-up compared with those prescribed apixaban (16% versus 6%).

problems.evidence: The cohort held 2.4% Asian patients against 14.4% in the trial, in a setting where Asian participants on warfarin had double the stroke or embolism risk of white participants. The composition difference is offered as the explanation for the gap between 0.98 and 0.79, but no transport or standardization was performed, and the confounding-control argument (matching to a standardized difference of 0.031) is entirely separate from the sampling argument that would license comparing the two estimates at all.
problems.quote: in ARISTOTLE, Asian participants experienced double the risk of stroke or SE when on warfarin therapy when compared with white participants

problems.evidence: Trial eligibility was applied by code search, and criteria that are poorly recorded pass silently: an unrecorded exclusion looks identical to one that was checked and not met. The paper adds the harder case, that recording may be differential by arm because tests such as renal function are more likely to be ordered before a treatment switch, which puts the misclassification on the exposure axis rather than symmetrically. The eligibility screen removed roughly 60% of the apixaban candidates, so its accuracy is not a minor matter.
problems.quote: Some of the criteria assessed for ARISTOTLE eligibility may not be well recorded in CPRD leading to a risk of misclassification.

problems.evidence: Warfarin quality was the scientific question, but time in therapeutic range exists only for warfarin users and only after baseline, and 13.3% of them had no INR at all and received a model-predicted value. The reported contrast against well-controlled warfarin, a death hazard ratio of 1.20 (1.04 to 1.37), is therefore a data-defined estimand conditioned on a post-baseline, one-arm, partly imputed variable, not a noisy version of a randomized comparison. The paper marks the result exploratory but reports it alongside the benchmarked estimates.
problems.quote: The analysis of TTR is limited by this being a post-baseline measure available for only 1 treatment arm leading to a risk of selection bias in this analysis

problems.evidence: The funnel runs from 86,888 apixaban and 159,632 warfarin patients to 41,487 and 101,159 after eligibility, to 9,120 after matching against the trial's aggregate baseline profile, to 8,846 pairs after propensity score matching. Ninety percent of the apixaban patients in the source data are gone before any outcome is counted, and the surviving cohort is defined by which trial characteristics could be matched: ethnicity and concomitant medications could not be, and are named as the reason the estimate diverges.
problems.quote: Selecting apixaban patients to match ARISTOTLE on key baseline characteristics yielded 9,120 apixaban patients (3,912 new users and 5,208 prevalent users) available for PSM to 101,159 warfarin patients.
problems.locator: Selection of ARISTOTLE-analogous CPRD Aurum Cohort

papers.title: In-silico trial emulation to predict the cardiovascular protection of new lipid-lowering drugs: an illustration through the design of the SIRIUS programme.
papers.one_line: A mechanistic atherosclerosis model applied to a virtual population matched to FOURIER enrollment is used to predict inclisiran's five-year effect on major adverse cardiovascular events before ORION-4 reads out, reporting hazard ratios with no confidence intervals and no p-values.
papers.what_was_done: A knowledge-based mechanistic model of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease was built from literature review and translated into differential equations covering a lipoprotein submodel (free PCSK9, LDL-C, HDL-C, VLDL-C and lipoprotein(a)) and a plaque growth and rupture submodel simulating one to three plaques across coronary, carotid and peripheral beds, with death after infarction or stroke drawn from an exponential law fit to a published Cox model built on the REACH registry. Virtual patients are parameter vectors; the virtual population was generated to match FOURIER enrollment characteristics, with statin and ezetimibe mix adjusted to recent practice. Calibration used one set of trial data and validation another, checked against ORION-11, FOURIER-OLE and ODYSSEY-OUTCOMES on three criteria: the observed hazard ratio inside the simulated 95% prediction percentile interval, the predicted hazard ratio inside the observed confidence interval, and at least 30% of the predicted interval falling inside the observed one, a threshold chosen empirically. Robustness used IMPROVE-IT and CANTOS. Uncertainty is summarized by bootstrapping 100 populations of 13,780 patients, a size chosen to match FOURIER. Because each virtual patient is its own control, sampling-theory tests are declared inapplicable, so no confidence intervals, p-values, multiplicity control or subgroup limits are reported. Recurrent events in a vascular bed are not simulated, and all ischemic strokes are attributed to carotid plaque rupture.

future_research.gap: The model is calibrated for population and subgroup predictions only; individual-level prediction would require a different calibration and validation exercise.
future_research.quote: To be able to generate reliable personalized predictions or risk scoring at an individual level, the current model would need to be modified and another set of calibration and validation would be required.

problems.evidence: The credibility argument is entirely about fidelity: the model must reproduce hazard ratios from ORION-11, FOURIER-OLE and ODYSSEY-OUTCOMES on held-out data, with an explicit separation of calibration from validation data to avoid tautology. Having passed that fidelity test, the model is then used for a causal claim it was never validated against, namely inclisiran's effect on major adverse cardiovascular events, an endpoint whose trials will not report before 2026. Reproducing observed distributions of past trial outputs is being treated as licence for a counterfactual prediction.
problems.quote: Data used for validation and robustness assessment must differ from data used for calibration, to avoid any risk of tautology.

problems.evidence: All reported uncertainty is a 95% prediction percentile interval from bootstrapping 100 subsamples, which covers parameter and inter-patient variability. The structural knowledge assumptions carry no interval at all and are adjudicated by a scientific committee. Sampling-theory inference is declared inapplicable, so no confidence interval, no p-value and no multiplicity or subgroup constraint accompanies any efficacy estimate. Diagnosable and undiagnosable uncertainty arrive in the reader's hands through the same single quantity.
problems.quote: In the in-silico paradigm interpretation, we assume that since we are not working in a sample of the population of interest but in a representation of the whole ASCVD population itself, the sampling theory-based statistical tests cannot apply.

problems.evidence: Confounding and randomization imbalance are declared removed because each virtual patient serves as its own control and the simulated environment fixes compliance, adherence and diet. What that establishes is internal consistency of the simulator, not that the parameter distributions and structural equations correspond to the population of interest. The label of trial emulation is carrying the identification argument here in the same way the target trial label does elsewhere.
problems.quote: Moreover, potential confounding variables are controlled as environment in simulations is perfectly defined (compliance, adherence, diet).

problems.evidence: The estimand is fixed by what could be calibrated rather than by the scientific question: because published trials report time to first event and give recurrences only in post hoc analyses, the model simulates one plaque per vascular bed and no recurrence, so the trial can only assess time to first event. The paper concedes this bears on cardiovascular death, to which recurrent events contribute. A comparable substitution puts every simulated ischemic stroke downstream of a carotid plaque rupture because the alternative submodels were not built.
problems.quote: Due to this unavailability of relevant published data for calibration/validation about recurrent events, the model does not simulate recurrent events in the same vascular bed and only one atheromatous plaque per vascular bed was modelled.

problems.evidence: The target population is defined by copying the enrollment profile of a past trial of a different agent, chosen because it spanned prior infarction, stroke and peripheral disease. The inclisiran effect that will be predicted for it is derived from ORION trials with an 18-month LDL-C endpoint, then extended to five-year event outcomes. Two transports are stacked, agent to agent and population to population, and neither is accompanied by a sampling assumption or an accounting of what would have to hold for the composed prediction to be valid.
problems.quote: We chose to generate a VPop matching patient's characteristics of the FOURIER study because it was a study investigating the efficacy of a PCSK9 inhibitor in secondary prevention encompassing the broad range of ASCVD phenotypes (prior MI, IS, and PAD).

problems.evidence: Everything a reader would need to check the emulation is deferred: the modelling and knowledge hypotheses, the calibration and validation results, and the underlying data are all promised in a separate manuscript in progress, with data otherwise available on request to the corresponding author. The equations, the parameter values and the virtual population generation procedure are not published alongside the design they support, and the sponsor reviewed and approved the knowledge models, the calibration strategy and the results.
problems.quote: Calibration and validation data used to generate the figures presented in the manuscript will be made available in the technical publication by Wang et al (in progress) and upon reasonable request to the corresponding author.

papers.title: Timing of follow-up visits after hospital discharge for COPD: Application of a new method.
papers.one_line: Among 94,034 Ontario patients discharged after a COPD hospitalization, random assignment to a follow-up-by-day-D strategy with censoring at discordance gave an all-cause hazard ratio of 1.03 (95% CI 1.01 to 1.05) at seven days and roughly 1 thereafter, with no beneficial window identified across 24 day thresholds.
papers.what_was_done: All Ontario residents aged 35 or older discharged from a hospitalization with COPD as a contributing diagnosis between 2004 and 2016 were identified in health administrative data, excluding those with a COPD admission in the prior year, palliative care, lung volume reduction surgery or transplant, or a stay over 21 days; 94,034 patients entered, of whom 73.5% saw a physician within 30 days. Rather than cloning, each patient was randomly assigned to one of two strategies, follow-up by day D or no follow-up by day D, then censored when observed care diverged from the assignment, with stabilized inverse probability of censoring weights estimated from a Cox model on roughly 25 baseline variables and outcomes compared by weighted Cox regression. The assignment was replicated ten times to check stability, and the whole procedure repeated for D from 7 through 30, giving 24 thresholds. The composite outcome over 180 days was all-cause emergency visit, readmission or death: adjusted hazard ratio 1.03 (1.01 to 1.05) at day 7, near 1 subsequently. The COPD-specific composite gave 0.97 (0.95 to 1.00) and stayed below 1. Death was also analyzed as a competing risk in Fine-Gray models. Neither analysis identified a beneficial follow-up window. Quality and comprehensiveness of the visit were not measured, nor were home care, non-physician visits or telephone contacts.

future_research.gap: The censoring weight model may omit variables that drive discordance between assigned and received follow-up, and the direction and size of the resulting bias is unknown.
future_research.quote: However, the validity of this approach assumed that we had all the variables necessary to do so.

problems.evidence: The design assigns a strategy label at random and then censors everyone whose actual care diverges, so identification rests entirely on the censoring weights, not on the coin flip. The paper nonetheless claims that unmeasured confounders are balanced as a consequence of random assignment, in the same discussion that concedes the weight model may be missing variables related to censoring. The emulation label is being read as delivering the assumption burden of a trial when the actual burden is no unmeasured confounding of a censoring process that touches most of the cohort.
problems.quote: Further, through randomization, unmeasured confounders were also balanced.

problems.evidence: Here the healthcare contact process is not a nuisance around the analysis, it is the exposure, and the composite outcome is built from emergency visits and readmissions, which are also contacts. The paper offers as an explanation of its null result that the visit lies on the causal pathway to the outcome, which makes exposure and outcome two draws from one encounter process. Nothing in the design models that process; it is handled by a censoring weight fit on baseline covariates.
problems.quote: A second explanation is that seeing a physician post-discharge is on the causal pathway to ED visit, hospital readmission and death making the physician visits and readmissions highly correlated and hazard ratios around 1 expected.

problems.evidence: The strategy is any ambulatory visit with any physician by a given day. A five-minute prescription renewal and a full post-discharge medication review enter the same arm, and post-discharge home care, non-physician visits and telephone follow-up are not captured at all. With a hazard ratio of 1.03 for the all-cause composite, a null of that size is exactly what averaging over an undefined mixture of treatment versions would produce, and no clinical criterion is offered for which visits belong together.
problems.quote: Third, we only focused on whether patients received a post discharge physician visit and the timing of the visit, we did not consider the quality or comprehensiveness of the care provided at the visit.

problems.evidence: Instead of picking one threshold, the entire procedure was rerun for every day from 7 to 30, and the lower bound was justified outcome-blind on the ground that visits before day 7 reflect the index admission rather than post-discharge care. That converts an arbitrary grid choice into a reported curve. It does not close the entry: no rule selects among the 24 estimates, no multiplicity accounting accompanies the scan, and the day-7 estimate of 1.03 is separately explained away as patients still unstable from the admission, which is a post-hoc reading of the curve.
problems.quote: To identify optimal timing of post discharge physician visit, the above steps were repeated 23 times, each time changing number of days that defined the groups were assigned to.

problems.evidence: Cohort entry is filtered on healthcare-use variables that are downstream of the same illness severity that drives both the exposure and the outcome: a COPD admission in the previous year, receipt of palliative services, and an index stay longer than 21 days. Each exclusion is justified explicitly by expected care needs or expected follow-up intensity, which is conditioning on a common effect of severity and of the visit process being studied. The remaining 94,034 patients are a severity-selected subset in a study whose exposure is care intensity.
problems.quote: Patients with inpatient length of stay greater than 21 days were excluded because they were more likely to have complicated hospital courses that would make close follow-up necessary.

problems.evidence: Uncertainty has two sources here, the censoring weights and the random assignment itself, and only the first enters the reported interval. The assignment was replicated ten times to check stability, but no rule is given for combining the ten replicates into the reported hazard ratio of 1.03 (1.01 to 1.05), and the same Monte Carlo variation applies independently at each of 24 thresholds. The interval quoted is a weighted Cox interval that treats one realized assignment as fixed.
problems.quote: To understand the stability of the randomization procedure, we replicated these steps ten times, each with a different randomization.

papers.title: Comparison of Methods of Clinical Trial Emulation Utilizing Data From the Comparison of AMD Treatment Trial (CATT) and the IRIS® Registry.
papers.one_line: Applying the CATT non-imaging eligibility criteria to 435,310 anti-VEGF-treated eyes in the IRIS Registry left 427 ranibizumab and 771 bevacizumab eyes, whose one-year visual acuity gains of 2 to 3 letters fell far below the 8.0 to 8.5 letters of the trial's monthly arms.
papers.what_was_done: Real-world arms were constructed from the American Academy of Ophthalmology IRIS Registry to stand against the two monthly arms of the Comparison of AMD Treatment Trial, using publicly released patient-level trial data. Of 435,310 treatment-naive eyes starting bevacizumab or ranibizumab between October 2015 and December 2019, application of all non-imaging trial inclusion and exclusion criteria plus the required pro re nata regimen left 427 ranibizumab and 771 bevacizumab eyes. Two adjustment methods were compared on the same eyes: one-to-one exact matching on age within five years, gender and baseline acuity within five letters, and inverse propensity score weighting on the same three variables. Exact matching found registry partners for 98% (281 of 286) of trial bevacizumab eyes and 87% (261 of 301) of trial ranibizumab eyes. The two methods agreed closely: ranibizumab 1.9 letters by matching versus 2.8 by weighting (P = 0.43), bevacizumab 2.4 versus 2.1 (P = 0.79), with injection counts of 9.0 versus 9.0 and 7.9 versus 7.7. Both fell well short of the trial monthly arms at 8.5 and 8.0 letters, with all P values 0.001. Visual acuity came from best documented Snellen readings converted by the formula 85 + 50 x log(Snellen fraction). Imaging criteria and anatomical outcomes could not be assessed, and clinical notes were not reviewed to confirm the regimen.

future_research.gap: Structured records cannot establish that pro re nata dosing was the intended regimen, so trials with such an arm may be poor emulation targets.
future_research.quote: future trial emulation studies may be better suited to clinical trials that do not have a prn treatment arm since true prn treatment is difficult to ascertain from structured EHR data alone

future_research.gap: Exact matching was affordable only because the registry is enormous; smaller source populations will need other methods, and none is identified.
future_research.quote: Other methodologies may be required for instances where the size of a source population for a study is limited.

problems.evidence: A registry holding more than 75 million patients and 1.6 million treated eyes yielded 1,198 analyzable eyes once trial eligibility and the regimen requirement were imposed, a survival rate below one in a thousand. The comparison that carries the paper is then built on 261 and 281 matched pairs. Database scale bought eligibility fidelity and delivered a sample smaller than the trial arms it was emulating.
problems.quote: Of the 1.6 million treatment-naive patient eyes treated with bevacizumab or ranibizumab in the IRIS Registry, <0.1% met all the nonimaging-based inclusion and exclusion criteria and followed the appropriate treatment regimen.

problems.evidence: The trial's anatomical entry criteria rest on optical coherence tomography and fluorescein angiography, and imaging is absent from the registry. Every retained eye is therefore treated as satisfying criteria that were never evaluated, and the same absence removes the anatomical outcomes. The eligibility screen that reduced the cohort to under 0.1% is explicitly the non-imaging subset, so the surviving cohort is defined by what the data happen to record.
problems.quote: Imaging data were not included and as a result, several anatomical inclusion and exclusion criteria in the CATT such as OCT and fluorescein angiography findings, as well as anatomical outcomes, could not be assessed.

problems.evidence: The pro re nata strategy was operationalized as a retina-specialist encounter every four to six weeks for a year plus at least one visit without an injection, a pattern rule that cannot distinguish intended as-needed dosing from irregular attendance. Registry ranibizumab eyes received more injections than the trial's own pro re nata arm yet gained fewer letters, which is what treatment-version heterogeneity inside a single named strategy looks like. No clinical criterion defines which observed injection patterns belong to the same strategy.
problems.quote: while we used a structured approach to define prn and monthly treatment, we did not review clinical notes to confirm treatment regimen

problems.evidence: The headline gap of roughly six letters is produced by a design that compares a real-world as-needed arm against a trial monthly arm, so scientific-target mismatch, mapping loss from Snellen conversion, and residual confounding are all folded into one number. The paper explicitly declines to read the gap as evidence that as-needed dosing is inferior, since the trial itself found otherwise, and attributes it to unmeasured factors. No decomposition separates the strategy difference from the measurement and confounding contributions.
problems.quote: Specifically, patient eyes in the CATT monthly treatment arms for ranibizumab and bevacizumab gained 8.5 and 8.0 letters respectively at 1 year compared with between 2 and 3 letters gained in the IRIS Registry prn treatment arms.

problems.evidence: Two adjustment methods were run head to head on identical eyes and the agreement is quantified: 1.9 versus 2.8 letters (P = 0.43) and 2.4 versus 2.1 letters (P = 0.79), with identical injection counts. That is the sensitivity-to-estimator demonstration the registry entry says is not required. The paper then explains the agreement away: restriction to under 0.1% of eyes left a cohort already comparable to the trial on the three matching variables, so weighting had little to adjust. The finding therefore says nothing about estimator choice in settings where overlap is imperfect.
problems.quote: This subgroup of patient eyes was comparable in age, gender, and baseline VA to the CATT monthly treatment arms, suggesting that IPSW may not have adjusted this overall cohort significantly.

problems.evidence: The primary outcome is an ETDRS letter count computed from best documented Snellen readings by a fixed formula, and Snellen charts in routine ophthalmology are not administered under trial conditions. The converted value enters the comparison against trial-measured acuity as an error-free number, with no error model and no propagation into the reported standard deviations of 14.0 to 16.0 letters, even though measurement conditions differ systematically between the two data sources being contrasted.
problems.quote: Because data from an EHR registry were used, clinical variables such as VA were not measured in a standardized fashion.

papers.title: Applying Trial Emulation Methods to Population-Scale Linked Electronic Health Records for Individuals with Multiple Long-Term Conditions Whilst Adjusting for Informative Observations.
papers.one_line: A conference abstract emulating ASCOT-BPLA in the Wales Multimorbidity e-cohort fits a Bayesian joint model of blood pressure that adjusts for the frequency of blood pressure observations, and reports no estimates.
papers.what_was_done: The Anglo-Scandinavian Cardiac Outcomes Trial Blood Pressure Lowering Arm, a randomized comparison of a calcium-channel-blocker regimen with a beta-blocker regimen, is used as the reference trial. The emulated cohort is drawn from population-scale linked anonymized electronic health records in the Wales Multimorbidity e-cohort and restricted to individuals who would have been eligible for the trial but who also have multiple long-term conditions, a group the trial did not represent. Outcomes are systolic and diastolic blood pressure predicted at treatment initiation, six weeks, three months, and six-monthly to four years. Estimation uses a fully probabilistic Bayesian joint model that allows for dropout due to death and is fit both with and without adjustment for how often blood pressure was recorded, the rationale being that patients with worse prognosis are seen more often. The claim that the joint model outperforms alternative adjustments on bias and coverage rests on previously published simulation work rather than on anything reported here. No cohort size, no estimate, no interval and no comparison against the trial result appear in the abstract, and the two model variants are not contrasted numerically.

problems.evidence: The observation process is elevated from an imputation nuisance to a modeled component: the joint model conditions on the number of available blood pressure measurements, on the stated ground that sicker patients are measured more often. That is a mechanism, not a diagnostic, and the abstract reports neither how much the adjusted and unadjusted fits differ nor what causal structure links measurement frequency to the treatment effect being emulated. Without a numerical contrast the visit process remains a modeling choice rather than a stated identifying assumption.
problems.quote: However, the Data Generating Mechanisms (DGMs) associated with EHR data mean that there is a need to adjust for informative observations, i.e. worse prognosis patients may have more observations.

problems.evidence: Death is handled inside the joint model as dropout rather than by censoring the blood pressure trajectory, which avoids the routine treatment of death as a data-cleaning step. What the four-year predicted blood pressure means for a person who has died is left unstated, and no alternative estimand such as a survivor-average or composite is named. The population is one with multiple long-term conditions, where mortality over four years is the dominant competing event.
problems.quote: Predictions were made using a fully probabilistic Bayesian joint model which allowed for dropout due to death and which either did or did not also adjust for the frequency of blood pressure observations available.

problems.evidence: The stated purpose is to carry a randomized result outward to a population the trial excluded, namely trial-eligible individuals who also have multiple long-term conditions, and the justification offered is that the electronic record contains such people. No benchmarking step against the trial estimate is described, so nothing establishes that a design validated on the trial question transfers to the multimorbid question. The methodological argument is entirely about the data-generating mechanism, not about the warrant for extrapolation.
problems.quote: Trial Emulation methods can be applied to Population-Scale Linked Electronic Health Records (EHR) to generalise the results of Randomised Controlled Trials (RCTs) to a broader patient population.

papers.title: Observational studies to emulate randomized trials: Some real-world barriers.
papers.one_line: Three randomized trial design features are shown to make emulation infeasible rather than merely noisy: forced discontinuation of prior treatment, run-in phases that exclude non-compliers, and studies of weaning off medication.
papers.what_was_done: Three design features are analyzed with worked trial examples and tabulated against what an observational database study can do. In IMPACT, 70% of enrolled patients were using inhaled-corticosteroid-containing inhalers and had to stop them on the day of randomization; the trial's stratified results give an exacerbation rate ratio of 0.71 (0.65 to 0.77) among prior corticosteroid users against 0.88 (0.76 to 1.03) among non-users, and an all-cause mortality hazard ratio of 0.63 (0.44 to 0.89) against 1.25 (0.60 to 2.59), so the trial estimate confounds initiation with forced withdrawal that no database study can impose. For run-in phases, the Heart Protection Study excluded 11,609 of 32,145 eligible subjects in a four-week placebo run-in leaving 20,536 randomized, and PARADIGM-HF excluded 1,102 and 977 across two successive run-ins leaving 8,442 of 10,513; the trial estimand is conditioned on tolerating the run-in and the emulation's is not. For weaning studies, withdrawal timing is defined at randomization in a trial but must be inferred forward in data using prescription durations plus a grace period; in a CPRD study of 125,441 triple-therapy initiators, 42,667 discontinued inhaled corticosteroids at a 60-day grace threshold, 74% of them restarted within one year, and 16% of the matched continuers stopped. WISDOM tapered the corticosteroid dose to zero over 12 weeks in 2,485 patients, which adds a further definitional problem.

future_research.gap: Trials intended to be complemented by real-world evidence could be designed so that their estimand is emulable, for example by adaptive selection designs that respect prior treatment.
future_research.quote: In conclusion, future randomized trials that aim to be emulated by observational studies could consider study designs that allow emulation and thus provide valid and complementary RWE.

future_research.gap: The three barriers are an incomplete list drawn from recent trials, with no procedure for enumerating the rest.
future_research.quote: It is important to first note that these design barriers are only some identified in recent randomized trials.

problems.evidence: Forced discontinuation at randomization is a protocol component with no observational counterpart, and its absence does not degrade the estimate, it changes the target. The trial measures initiation plus withdrawal of prior therapy; the emulation measures initiation with prior therapy continued. The IMPACT stratified results size the difference: an exacerbation rate ratio of 0.71 among prior corticosteroid users against 0.88 among non-users, and mortality 0.63 against 1.25. Any benchmarking exercise across that pair is comparing two different estimands.
problems.quote: -Effect measure includes the effect of study treatment initiation and of discontinued prior treatments

problems.evidence: A run-in used to screen out non-compliers restricts the randomized estimand to those who tolerated the run-in treatment, while the emulation estimates the effect among all selected subjects. In the Heart Protection Study that is 20,536 people rather than 32,145; in PARADIGM-HF, 8,442 rather than 10,513. When such an emulation disagrees with its trial, nothing in current practice separates that scientific-target mismatch from confounding, mapping loss or estimation error, and the paper notes that observational studies are usually the ones blamed.
problems.quote: -Effect measure includes effect of study treatment initiation, only among subjects who tolerated the run-in treatment and remained for random allocation

problems.evidence: For weaning studies the trial assigns discontinuation at randomization while the database study must construct it from prescription durations, so continuation and discontinuation are algorithm outputs rather than clinical states. The CPRD example shows the classes do not hold: at a 60-day grace threshold 42,667 patients were labeled discontinuers, 74% restarted within a year, and 16% of the matched continuers stopped. Dose tapering, as in the 12-week corticosteroid taper in WISDOM, has no representation in the class scheme at all.
problems.quote: -Create groups of users who continue or discontinue the study treatment (must look ‘into the future’ to define continuation and discontinuation, and subjects may restart)

problems.evidence: Defining discontinuation requires looking forward across a prescription duration plus a grace period chosen to absorb variation in physician and pharmacy visits, and the person-time inside that window cannot contribute to the effect. The emulated effect therefore begins only after the look-forward period ends, unlike the trial effect which begins at randomization. No outcome-blind rule sets the grace period; 60 days was the value used in the worked CPRD example and 74% of those it labeled discontinuers restarted.
problems.quote: -Effect measure includes effect of weaning off study treatment, only beyond the ‘into the future’ period of follow-up

problems.evidence: Three named, checkable trial design features are offered as grounds on which an emulation should not proceed, which converts part of the fitness question from narrative into a list a reviewer can apply before any data are pulled. The list is on the trial side rather than the data side: it says nothing about whether a given database supports a question with no such feature, it is explicitly incomplete, and no threshold governs the intermediate cases such as a run-in that homogenizes therapy rather than screening compliance.
problems.quote: Even so, some RCT design aspects cannot be emulated, described below and summarized in the Table 1.

problems.evidence: The barriers are presented as some of those visible in recent trials, with no characterization of the class of questions that can be emulated and no way to know whether a fourth or fifth barrier applies to the next question. Initiatives that read agreement across 32 trial-emulation pairs as evidence about the method are therefore averaging over a set whose emulable and non-emulable members were never separated on principled grounds.
problems.quote: It is important to first note that these design barriers are only some identified in recent randomized trials.

papers.title: Emulation of randomized trials of direct oral anticoagulants with claims data and implications for new Factor XI inhibitors.
papers.one_line: Eight RCT-DUPLICATE emulations of direct oral anticoagulant trials all met binary statistical significance agreement with a Pearson correlation of 0.92 (0.61 to 0.99), and this record is offered as grounds for expecting database studies to substitute for future Factor XI inhibitor trials.
papers.what_was_done: Eight of the 32 RCT-DUPLICATE emulations concerned direct oral anticoagulants against other anticoagulants. Each database protocol was developed iteratively through prespecified checks of feasibility, power and covariate balance, and registered on clinicaltrials.gov before treatment-stratified outcome counts were examined. Agreement was scored on three prespecified binary metrics: statistical significance agreement, defined as estimates and intervals on the same side of the null with a partial grade for meeting noninferiority criteria; estimate agreement, defined as the emulation estimate falling inside the trial's 95% interval; and standardized difference agreement at Z below 1.96. All eight pairs met significance agreement, six fully and two partially, and all but the EINSTEIN-PE pair met the other two, with a Pearson correlation of 0.92 (0.61 to 0.99) across the eight. The EINSTEIN-PE discordance is argued away by appeal to its sister trial: EINSTEIN-DVT gave HR 0.68 (0.44 to 1.04) and EINSTEIN-PE gave 1.12 (0.75 to 1.68), the prespecified pooled trial analysis gave 0.89 (0.66 to 1.19), and a six-trial meta-analysis gave pooled RR 0.92 (0.80 to 1.07), so the emulations are said to track the trial evidence rather than the single outlier. A two-stage extension is proposed: benchmark against phase III Factor XI trials, then use the calibrated infrastructure for supplemental indications.

future_research.gap: Whether a design and analytics infrastructure calibrated on one drug class can answer the ten or more supplemental-indication questions expected for a new class is posed as an open question.
future_research.quote: Understanding concordance in results between an RCT-database study pair requires nuanced and critical thinking about the alignment of research questions, the suitability of data and design, and must be interpreted in light of expected discordance even between trial pairs.
future_research.locator: Nuanced evaluation of the concordance of RCT and database study results

problems.evidence: The argument runs directly from eight successful anticoagulant emulations to an expectation about a drug class with a different mechanism whose trials have not read out, and the warrant offered is similarity of context, indication and outcome. No theory connects the two: the eight replications concern warfarin comparisons in atrial fibrillation and venous thromboembolism, while the proposed questions are supplemental indications for Factor XI inhibitors. The proposed two-stage calibration would extend the same reasoning, benchmarking on phase III trials and then relying on the infrastructure for questions no trial covers.
problems.quote: it is highly likely that similarly robust insights could be generated from database studies for Factor XI inhibitors
problems.locator: Implications for future clinical evidence generation of Factor XI inhibitors

problems.evidence: Agreement is scored on three binary metrics, and the coarseness shows in the tally: six full and two partial significance agreements, where partial means only that a noninferiority criterion was met while the better-powered database study indicated superiority. Estimate agreement asks whether one point falls inside the other's interval, which rewards imprecise trials. The only continuous summary reported is a Pearson correlation of 0.92 across eight pairs, with an interval from 0.61 to 0.99, which describes rank co-movement of eight numbers rather than calibration of the estimands.
problems.quote: The results for each RCT-database study pair were compared using pre-specified binary metrics for agreement including statistical significance agreement, estimate agreement, and standardized difference agreement.

problems.evidence: Regulators and health technology assessment bodies have issued guidance on how database studies may enter evidence packages, and the stated obstacle is that decision makers have no way to judge whether a particular study yields valid causal inference. The proposed remedy is a per-class calibration exercise, which presupposes an available trial and supplies no threshold for adequate emulation or acceptable residual confounding in the cases where none exists. The gap is diagnosed as a decision-maker capability problem rather than as a missing standard.
problems.quote: some hesitate to consider non-randomized studies as they find it difficult to assess whether a given database study will provide valid causal inferences

problems.evidence: Registration of the full protocol before treatment-stratified outcome counts were examined blocks the most direct route by which a target trial is selected after seeing the answer, and it is stronger than registering a protocol alone because the recorded boundary is the outcome data rather than the study start. It does not close the entry: the protocols were developed iteratively against feasibility, power and balance checks run on the same database, so the design is conditioned on the data even though it is not conditioned on the outcome.
problems.quote: Importantly, the full protocols, including details of the data checks conducted to date, were pre-registered on clinicaltrials.gov before examining treatment-stratified outcome counts or conducting inferential analyses.

problems.evidence: Fitness is assessed by a named sequence of prespecified checks on feasibility, power and balance on key confounders, run before inferential analysis, which is more than a narrative claim that the data suit the question. What the checks require is not stated, no threshold is quoted for any of the three, and no study is reported as having been stopped by them, so whether the gate can fail remains untested in what is presented.
problems.quote: Each database study protocol was iteratively developed, going through a series of pre-specified data checks to evaluate feasibility, power, and balance on key confounders.
